notable_absence.finding: Two absences, both structural rather than incidental. (1) No version, anywhere. The page introduces a named feature with the phrase 'In Couchbase Server, early filtering, early ordering, and early pagination provide another line of defense' and never says since when. Every other page in this batch that introduces an optimisation dates it (index_pushdowns.md dates index projection to 5.0, MIN/MAX pushdown to 5.5, skip-key range scan to 6.5; groupby-aggregate-performance.md dates group/aggregate pushdown to 5.5), so early filtering is the one member of this family with no availableSince obtainable from its own page. A reader cannot tell whether it is new in 8.0 or years old. (2) The Limitations section governs early ORDERING AND PAGINATION only - it sits under the 'Early Order and Pagination' heading and its first sentence says 'The optimizer only selects early ordering and pagination when the following conditions are met'. There is no corresponding list for early FILTERING. The page shows early filtering working in Examples 3 and 4 and never states when the optimizer will or will not choose it, so half the feature is documented by conditions and half by example only. This is the same asymmetry in reverse to the one the 7.2 record noticed about undated limitations.

cross_component_finding: This is the only page in the batch that names all three services in one place and assigns each a role in the same pipeline (Index service applies spans and pushdowns; Query service applies early filters, order and pagination; Data service serves the fetch), which makes it the load-bearing page for the whole family - covering-indexes.md never names the Query service at all. Two component couplings are stated here and nowhere else in the batch: (a) 'When early ordering is in effect, parallelism is turned off' ties an index-scan strategy to n1ql:max-parallelism, a Query service setting documented in a different module, and the coupling is one-directional - the query settings documentation is not told that early ordering can override it; (b) 'it does not support reverse index scan' attributes a hard capability limit to the Index service in a subordinate clause, on a page about the Query service's workaround. The reverse-scan limitation is the reason for a documented behaviour in at least three pages (this one, index_pushdowns.md's index-order section, and by implication groupby-aggregate-performance.md's ordering rules) and it has no page of its own; the 7.2 extraction of index_pushdowns.md recorded exactly this as a notable absence, and it is still absent in 8.0 - what changed is that this page now explains why, in seven words.
cross_product_finding: The page is near-identical to cloud/indexes/early-filters-and-pagination.md (already extracted) and to server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/early-filters-and-pagination.md, with the same two example indexes (idx_eat_city_name, idx_landmark_city_name) and the same eight examples; the Capella copy differs only in substituting 'Couchbase Capella therefore attempts to apply filters, order, and pagination before fetching data' for this page's 'Couchbase Server therefore attempts...'. Two things worth phase 2's attention. First, the module moved between 7.2 and 8.0: in 7.2 this content lived under learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/, in 8.0 under indexes/, so the corpus holds the same page under three page_ids and its vocabulary will look three times as recurrent as it is. Second, the earlier Capella record for this page supports its order-pushdown relation with an evidence string that splices two non-adjacent sentences with an ellipsis ('...ordering cannot be pushed down to the Index service. ... So in this case, early ordering, limit, and offset are done by the Query service before fetch.'); that string is not verbatim on the page and would be refused by the current write-time gate, so at least one pre-gate record in the corpus carries evidence the gate would now reject. I recorded the same fact here from a single contiguous sentence instead.
